name: Elvis Presley
hook: The singer whose first single, a blues song played at twice the speed, made Sun Records and then RCA the centre of rock and roll.

blurb.age13: Elvis Presley was born in Tupelo, Mississippi, in 1935 and grew up in Memphis. In July 1954, at Sun Studio, he and two musicians started fooling around with an old blues song, 'That's All Right' by Arthur Crudup, and played it much faster. Sam Phillips recorded it. A Memphis radio DJ played it over and over the same week. Within two years Elvis was the most famous singer in the world.
blurb.adult: Born in Tupelo in 1935. 'That's All Right' was recorded on 5 July 1954 with Scotty Moore on electric guitar and Bill Black on string bass, and issued as Sun 209 on 19 July with the bluegrass song 'Blue Moon of Kentucky' on the B-side: a Black songwriter's blues and a white country song on one record. Arthur Crudup, who wrote 'That's All Right' and recorded it for RCA in 1946, stopped recording in the 1950s over unpaid royalties; a 1968 agreement for $60,000 fell through when the publisher, Hill and Range, would not sign, and by 1971 he had collected a little over $10,000 (Wikipedia's article on Crudup). He died in 1974. RCA bought Presley's contract in 1955 and 'Heartbreak Hotel' (1956) was his first national number one. He died in 1977.
